terra.problem: The passage says the women saw how Jesus' body was placed, not that they watched Joseph handle all of it.
No one had been laid in the tomb before, but that does not establish that the space was brand new.
Comparing Jesus' burial tomb to a fresh pan makes a light comparison out of a death and burial.
The passage says the women saw the tomb and how the body was placed; it does not say they paid attention to every detail.
The passage does not say the rolled-away stone was the first thing the women saw.
Saying it was just the women, their spices and the tomb asserts that no one else was there. The passage does not establish that.
The passage says the women bowed their faces, but it does not say they did not reach out.
The men say Jesus has risen; the passage does not establish the broader claim that His body did not go anywhere because someone carried it.
The passage says the women reported what happened, not that they could not keep it to themselves.
“That has to sting” presents a feeling about the women's experience as fact rather than as Papa Dorin's guess.
Saying the apostles heard nonsense turns the passage's statement that the words seemed like nonsense to them into a claim that the report was nonsense.
The passage says the women's words seemed like nonsense to the apostles, not that the others called them nonsense.
The passage says Peter ran to the tomb; it does not say he did not look for anyone.
